Project Manager – Large Projects Administrative Project Management Focus Position Summary The Project Manager – Large Projects is responsible for the administrative coordination, governance, documentation, tracking, and reporting required to support large, complex projects.

This role ensures that project information is organized, timelines are visible, actions are tracked, risks and issues are documented, and stakeholders have accurate information to support decision-making. This role does not own solution design, deployment strategy, customer adoption, operational readiness, or business execution.

Instead, the Project Manager provides the structure, cadence, documentation, and administrative discipline needed to keep large projects organized and transparent.

This is an individual contributor role that works closely with project sponsors, workstream owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, commercial teams, operations, finance, legal, quality, supply chain, digital, and other stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities: Project Administration and Coordination Maintain project plans, timelines, milestones, action trackers, decision logs, risk logs, issue logs, and dependency trackers. Coordinate project meetings, governance forums, steering committee reviews, and stakeholder update sessions.

Prepare meeting agendas, capture minutes, document decisions, and follow up on assigned actions. Ensure project documentation is complete, current, organized, and accessible to appropriate stakeholders. Support consistent use of project templates, tools, trackers, and reporting formats.

Governance Support Support project governance by maintaining meeting cadence, escalation records, approval documentation, and decision history. Track required approvals, sign-offs, stage gates, and governance checkpoints. Ensure project sponsors and workstream owners have accurate information for reviews and decisions.

Maintain visibility to open decisions, overdue actions, unresolved issues, and upcoming milestones. Help ensure governance processes are followed consistently across large projects. Timeline and Milestone Tracking Maintain the master project timeline based on input from workstream owners and accountable business leads.

Track progress against milestones, deliverables, and agreed due dates. Identify and flag timeline variances, overdue items, and dependency gaps for review by accountable owners. Consolidate updates from multiple workstreams into a single project view. Support visibility to critical path items without owning execution of the underlying work.

Reporting and Communication Support Prepare project status reports, dashboards, executive summaries, and stakeholder updates. Consolidate inputs from workstream owners, deployment leaders, finance, operations, commercial teams, and other functions.

Ensure project reports clearly reflect status, milestones, risks, issues, decisions needed, and next steps. Maintain accurate records of project communications and leadership updates. Support consistent and timely information flow across project stakeholders. Risk, Issue, and Action Tracking Maintain risk, issue, action, and dependency logs.

Document risk descriptions, issue status, owners, target dates, mitigation updates, and escalation history. Follow up with accountable owners to obtain updates and closure status. Flag overdue actions, unresolved issues, or missing information to project sponsors or designated leads.

Support escalation documentation but does not own resolution of technical, operational, commercial, or deployment issues. Budget and Resource Administration Track project budget information, purchase orders, invoices, resource assumptions, and financial updates as directed by finance or project sponsors.

Consolidate budget and resource inputs for project reporting. Maintain documentation related to project spend, approvals, forecasts, and financial decisions. Support administrative coordination of vendor documentation, contracts, statements of work, and related records.

Flag missing financial information, pending approvals, or budget variances for review by accountable owners. Documentation and Records Management Maintain organized project repositories, files, version control, and document naming standards.

Ensure key project documents, approvals, meeting records, reports, and governance materials are stored appropriately. Support audit readiness by maintaining clear records of decisions, approvals, risks, changes, and status updates. Capture lessons learned and archive project materials at project close.

Support continuous improvement of project administration tools, templates, and documentation practices. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, project management, life sciences, engineering, or related field preferred.

Experience supporting large projects, complex initiatives, project management offices, commercial operations, business operations, or administrative project coordination. Strong skills in project documentation, meeting coordination, status reporting, action tracking, and records management.

Ability to consolidate information from multiple stakeholders into clear, accurate project updates. Strong organizational skills and attention to detail. Ability to manage multiple deadlines, documents, trackers, and reporting cycles. Strong written and verbal communication skills.

Proficiency with project management, collaboration, reporting, and productivity tools. Ability to work in a matrixed organization and follow up with stakeholders across functions and levels. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting large customer, commercial, operational, supply chain, digital, or transformation projects.

Experience in life sciences, pharmaceutical, biopharma, healthcare, diagnostics, laboratory, manufacturing, or regulated environments. Familiarity with project governance, PMO practices, stage-gate processes, and executive reporting.

Experience with tools such as Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams, Power BI, CRM, ERP, or similar platforms. Understanding of budget tracking, purchase order processes, vendor documentation, or contract administration. Project management certification or training preferred but not required.

Key Competencies Project administration Documentation management Meeting coordination Status reporting Timeline tracking Action-item follow-up Risk and issue logging Governance support Records management Attention to detail Stakeholder follow-up Tool and tracker discipline Scope and Impact The Project Manager – Large Projects is an individual contributor role focused on the administrative management of large, complex projects.

The role supports project transparency, governance discipline, documentation quality, leadership visibility, and timely follow-up. The role does not own solution deployment, customer adoption, operational readiness, business execution, technical solution design, or commercial strategy.

Accountability for those activities remains with designated business owners, Solution Deployment Leaders, Solution Architects, commercial leaders, and functional teams. Travel Requirements Limited travel may be required for project meetings, governance sessions, workshops, or site-based coordination.

Compensation and Benefits The salary range estimated for this position based in California is $112,500.00–$168,500.00. This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy.

Sponsor-Dedicated - Fully Home Based anywhere in US

Within this sponsor, the Clinical Trial Leader (CTL) serves at the Senior Project Manager level and plays a pivotal leadership role within the Clinical Delivery Team. This position provides strategic global oversight , driving alignment, direction, and accountability across Phase II and III clinical trials conducted worldwide. The CTL ensures precise planning, efficient execution, and high-quality delivery of trials that bring speed and value to patients and investigative sites.
Operating across multi-country, multi-regional trials, the CTL provides strong global project management leadership , ensuring milestones, KPIs, and strategic objectives are met. Therapeutic areas include Immunology, Metabolic, and Oncology. Candidates must have extensive Project Management experience leading Phase II & III trials globally, with proven ability to influence and guide diverse teams.

Global Trial Preparation
Lead global planning activities and operational feasibility assessments, ensuring timelines and strategies are realistic and globally aligned.
Strengthen cross-functional cohesion by working onsite with colleagues in Statistics, Data Management, Medical Writing, Site Monitoring, Quality, and Regulatory.
Guide country allocation and feasibility processes, helping shape global site strategies with operational insight.
Develop robust global engagement, recruitment, and risk mitigation plans informed by patient, site, and regional feedback.
Lead vendor outsourcing strategy—identification, evaluation, and scope-of-work development—ensuring global operational readiness.
Bring teams together onsite to harmonize trial processes across clinical quality, safety, investigational product management, and financial planning.
Prepare or support responses to regulatory and ethics authorities across regions.
Ensure global teams are trained, aligned, and equipped for execution.
Global Trial Conduct
Maintain high-level oversight of worldwide trial operations, ensuring compliance with GCP, SOPs, and diverse regional regulations.
Monitor global patient recruitment, risks, timelines, and budgets, driving issue resolution through clear leadership.
Direct documentation changes, study amendments, and retraining across all regions and functions.
Provide strong oversight of global vendors, central labs, and external partners, ensuring consistent performance.
Serve as the connective tissue across global clinical delivery, fostering open communication and unity of purpose.
Coordinate biomarker, genomic, and sub-study activities for applicable early-phase trials, often requiring cross-regional alignment.
Trial Closeout & Reporting
Provide global leadership through data cleaning, database lock, and closeout activities.
Support CTR development and ensure timely global registry disclosure.
Ensure completeness and accuracy of the Trial Master File (TMF) across all participating regions.
Support scientific publications and global communication of study outcomes.
Strategic Contributions
Partner with portfolio leaders to provide operational and scientific insight that shapes global study strategy.
Elevate risks, bottlenecks, and insights to the Evidence Team to drive swift, coordinated solutions.
Lead or contribute to global feasibility assessments that influence trial design, operational models, and regional planning.

Required
Bachelor’s degree (4-year undergraduate degree).
Proven experience providing global leadership across Phase II & III clinical trials.
Therapeutic area experience in Immunology, Metabolic, or Oncology.
Deep understanding of global clinical trial planning, execution, and regulatory landscapes.
Exceptional leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills across complex, matrixed, multicultural environments.
Ability to lead through influence, anticipate global challenges, and ensure patient-focused outcomes.
Core Competencies
Global Leadership: Confidently guide teams across regions, cultures, and functions; set vision, instill accountability, and shape high-performing global execution.
Strategic Mindset: Think several steps ahead, anticipate challenges, and align global strategies with portfolio needs.
Project Management Excellence: Expert in global timelines, risk mitigation, cross-functional coordination, issue escalation, and solution delivery.
Collaboration & Influence: Build trust across continents; unify teams through clear direction and inspiring presence onsite.
High-Impact Communication: Transparent, diplomatic, and culturally attuned communicator who elevates team performance.

This is not a traditional project management role — it is a chance to be at the center of global clinical delivery. As a Senior Global Project Manager / Clinical Trial Leader, you will be a visible, influential leader driving the success of trials that span continents. The hybrid model gives you the best of both worlds: meaningful onsite collaboration that strengthens team cohesion, paired with the flexibility of remote work.
You will shape strategy, drive execution, and help deliver therapies that change lives. Your leadership will connect people, processes, and science — ensuring trials advance efficiently, ethically, and with global impact.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

About Wolt
At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.
Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Every contact that reaches a customer support agent, and every credit issued to customers, represents a defect somewhere in our system. This role exists to help find those defects, trace them to their source, and work with the teams responsible to eliminate them at a systemic level.
This is a high impact senior program management role within the EMEA Customer Experience organisation, reporting to the Director of Defect Elimination and Customer Experience. The Senior Program Manager is accountable for turning customer experience signals from Wolt and/or Deliveroo markets into clear, actionable insight, and for driving the resulting fixes through to resolution with partner teams.
What you’ll be doing
You will own the delivery of the defect elimination program across EMEA, including application of the defect driver taxonomy to identify where defect rate concentrates, and where customer outcomes are worst. You will build a clear, prioritised list of issues for partner teams to work through.
You will represent the voice of the customer in the rooms where decisions get made about your markets. That means preparing and presenting data in product reviews, weekly/monthly business reviews and planning sessions, so the cost of poor customer experience is concrete and attributable, and so partner teams understand what is being asked of them and why.
You will build working relationships with partner teams in engineering, marketplace operations, courier operations, and finance, and you will track the fixes they commit to through to completion. You will feed results back into the program so everyone can see what worked, and to ensure defects are eliminated for good.
You will maintain and improve the data infrastructure and reporting that underpins this work, ensuring customer experience insights are credible, available and actionable.
Our humble expectations
The right person for this role has spent time inside a large-scale customer experience or operations function, and has direct experience translating customer defects through identification, root cause analysis and resolution. They are comfortable working with imperfect data, and they know how to build a credible case when the evidence is directional rather than conclusive.
Strong analytical instincts are essential. This person needs to know what questions to ask of the data and whether the answers make sense. Prior exposure to a successful voice of the customer (VoC) program is critical.
There is a meaningful cross-functional dimension to the role. This person will spend real time getting other teams to prioritise work that benefits the customer but may compete with other priorities. That requires good judgement, clear communication, and the ability to build trust quickly with people outside their reporting line.
The role also requires the ability to drive results in a dynamic and ambiguous landscape. The right person will combine introducing structure and rigor, while being agile and responsive to changing priorities and emerging issues.
This is a high impact and high visibility role, with the opportunity to interact with stakeholders and teams across the full customer lifecycle. The role will also span across 40 EMEA Roo & Wolt markets, meaning there is an opportunity to drive financial and customer experience results at scale.
Next steps
You will first meet with our Talent Acquisition team to understand role and company fit. Then, you will meet with the Hiring Manager who will talk through your relevant experience and ask you competency based questions that assess your suitability for the role.

The third stage is an assignment, where you will be given a business problem to think through, and present back to the team. If successful, there may be a final conversation with a more senior stakeholder. Throughout all stages, you will have plenty of opportunities to ask any questions about the role, team or company.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We’re committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That’s why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

The Agile Delivery Manager (ADM) is accountable for delivering business value across one or more agile teams, specifically in support of the organization’s digital transformation.

Acting as a servant leader and connector between strategic intent and operational execution, the ADM sits at the bridge point between the product/feature layer (Product Owners, Business Analysts, Business Owners) and the delivery layer (Engineering Managers, Developers, QA, and the Scrum Masters who own team-level performance).

The ADM ensures that delivery aligns with product roadmaps, value streams, and enterprise priorities.
This role is not about managing tasks—it’s about enabling flow, clarity, and measurable outcomes that advance the organization’s customer and business goals. The ADM owns the health and predictability of the Program Increment (PI): making sure it is planned well, tracked honestly, and delivered against — while escalating risks and dependencies before they become blockers. .

s.h: The role is responsible for the following results
s.t:
Delivery Flow and Value
Consistently leveraging lean and agile practices to achieve outcomes, not just complete output.
Orchestrate planning and coordination activities across multiple teams, including PI Planning, Scrum of Scrums and cross-team synchronization, and protecting the teams against interference and over commitment, to sustain focus and health velocity.
Advise Product Owners and Business Analysts in backlog management and sequencing to ensure clear cross-team prioritization.
Monitor flow and delivery health metrics (predictability, throughput, cycle time, PI objective achievement) and share them with teams to celebrate progress and surface improvement opportunities
Use performance and progress data to increase transparency and predictability in meeting commitments to the business.
Facilitate the adoption and evolution of agile practices to continuously improve how the organization produces high quality and high value outcomes.
Align teams with strategic goals through transparent sequencing of work, clear identification of cross-team dependencies; own the identification, tracking, and mitigation of delivery risks and issues, ensuring timely resolution or escalation.
Facilitate scaled/cross-team agile events (e.g., PI Planning, System Demo, Inspect & Adapt, Scrum of Scrums) so they are productive and time-boxed, setting a consistent standard of effectiveness across teams. Team-level ceremonies remain owned by Scrum Masters. Ensure delivery standards and definitions of done are applied consistently across the teams.
Enablement & Coaching
Coach Scrum Masters, Business Owners, Product Owners and Business Analysts to communicated in terms of value delivered rather than requirement fulfillment.
Guide continuous improvement through retrospectives, delivery health checks, and root-cause analysis at the multi-team and PI Levels
Build agile maturity through mentoring, modeling psychological safety, and reenforcing learning cycles.
Stakeholder Engagement
Translate delivery progress into business impact, reporting what value was realized, not just completed.
Own upward and outward communication of delivery status, risks, and PI outcomes to executives, business owners, the Governance & Transformation Lead, and technology leadership.
Ensure the “voice of delivery” is represented in strategic planning and portfolio discussions.

PI predictability (planned vs. delivered PI objectives) across teams in scope.
Flow metrics trend (cycle time, throughput, work-in-progress) shared and improving over time.
Time-to-resolution on escalated risks, issues, and cross-team dependencies.
Stakeholder-reported clarity and trust in delivery commitments (Business Owners, executive sponsors).
Team-reported psychological safety and agile maturity progression.

Our commercial organization supports a diverse portfolio of merchants, ranging from strategic Enterprise partners to thousands of small and medium-sized businesses. Successfully serving both requires a combination of high-touch relationship management and scalable commercial programs.
We're looking for a Commercial Program Manager who will directly own a portfolio of Enterprise merchant relationships while also leading programs that improve how we support, engage, and grow our long-tail SMB business.

At the same time, you will lead programs designed to improve how Uber manages thousands of SMB merchants at scale. Rather than directly managing the SMB long tail, you'll build and optimize the programs, processes, segmentation strategies, reporting, automation, and commercial playbooks that enable Account Managers and Account Coordinators to effectively manage large books of business.

Lead commercial conversations and negotiations while balancing merchant objectives with Uber's broader business priorities.
Partner cross-functionally across Operations, Product, Marketing, Sales, and other teams to resolve merchant challenges and unlock growth.

Standardize workflows, playbooks, and operating processes across large merchant portfolios.

Als Regional Trade Manager übernimmst du eine Schlüsselrolle an der Schnittstelle von Sales, Marketing Schweiz und Product Management.

Du übersetzt globale Strategien in wirksame regionale Aktivierungsmassnahmen, unterstützt den Vertrieb mit relevanten Verkaufsargumentationen und sorgst dafür, dass die Bedürfnisse unserer Partner und Märkte gezielt in die Organisation zurückfliessen.

* Du konzipierst und steuerst regionale Promotions, Partneraktivierungen, Events und B2B-Kampagnen und entwickelst daraus nachhaltige Aktivierungsformate mit langfristiger Wirkung
* Markt-, Partner- und Wettbewerbsinformationen analysierst du systematisch und leitest daraus konkrete Handlungsempfehlungen für Product Management, Sales Leadership und Marketing ab
### **Das bringst du für die Stelle mit** ###
* Du bringst mehrere Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-Sales mit. Ob im direkten oder indirekten Vertrieb: Du hast vertriebs- oder marketingnahe Konzepte erfolgreich entwickelt und umgesetzt sowie nachweisbare Erfolge erzielt. Erfahrungen im B2B- oder Trade Marketing, Retail- oder Category Management sowie erste Führungserfahrungen in der Leitung von Teams oder Projekten sind willkommen

* CRM, Kampagnensteuerung und Reporting sind für dich mehr als nur Instrumente. Du nutzt Daten gezielt, um Chancen zu identifizieren, Entscheidungen zu treffen und Massnahmen messbar erfolgreicher zu machen
* Mit deinen überzeugenden Kommunikations- und Präsentationsfähigkeiten gelingt es dir, Sales Teams zu begeistern, Stakeholder mitzunehmen und nachhaltige Beziehungen zu internen wie externen Partnern aufzubauen
* Du bewegst dich sicher zwischen Marketing, Sales und Product Management und findest auch bei unterschiedlichen Interessen tragfähige Lösungen
* Du kommunizierst stilsicher in Deutsch. Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil und helfen dir, in einem schweizweiten Umfeld noch wirkungsvoller zu agieren

Aufgaben
Darauf kannst du dich bei uns freuen
Keine 08/15-Projekte

Bei uns entwickelst du HLS-Lösungen für außergewöhnliche Infrastrukturprojekte wie Schleusen, Wehranlagen, Schiffshebewerke und bewegliche Brücken. Das bedeutet: besondere technische Anforderungen, ungewöhnliche Rahmenbedingungen und Projekte, die man nicht jeden Tag auf dem Tisch hat.
Projekte von der ersten Idee bis zur Umsetzung

**Technische Berechnungen und Auslegung
**Du führst erforderliche Berechnungen durch, legst Anlagen und Komponenten aus und dimensionierst diese entsprechend den technischen Anforderungen des jeweiligen Projekts.
Planungs- und Ausschreibungsunterlagen
Du erstellst Planungsunterlagen, Leistungsbeschreibungen und Leistungsverzeichnisse und schaffst damit eine belastbare Grundlage für Ausschreibung, Vergabe und Ausführung.
Abstimmung mit allen Projektbeteiligten
Du stimmst deine Planung mit Auftraggebern, Architekten, Fachplanern, unseren internen Planungsteams sowie ausführenden Unternehmen ab und sorgst dafür, dass Schnittstellen frühzeitig erkannt und sinnvoll gelöst werden.
Begleitung der Bauausführung
Auch nach Abschluss der Planung bleibst du am Projekt: Du unterstützt bei technischen Fragestellungen während der Ausführung, prüfst die Umsetzung und begleitest Projekte bis zur erfolgreichen Fertigstellung.
Eigenständige Projektbearbeitung
Je nach Erfahrung übernimmst du Schritt für Schritt mehr Verantwortung und bearbeitest deine Projekte perspektivisch eigenständig.
Qualifikation
Mit diesem Profil bist du die ideale Ergänzung für unser Team
Du hast ein Studium im Bereich Versorgungstechnik, Gebäudetechnik, Energietechnik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung abgeschlossen oder verfügst als Techniker oder Meister im Bereich HLS / SHK über eine entsprechende Qualifikation.
Idealerweise hast du bereits Erfahrung in der Planung von Heizungs-, Lüftungs- oder Sanitäranlagen gesammelt.

Du besitzt ein ausgeprägtes technisches Verständnis und suchst Lösungen, die nicht nur planerisch richtig sind, sondern sich auch in der Praxis umsetzen lassen.
Du arbeitest selbstständig, strukturiert und lösungsorientiert und behältst auch bei technisch anspruchsvollen Aufgaben den Überblick.
Gleichzeitig kommunizierst du offen und klar und arbeitest gerne mit unterschiedlichen Fachdisziplinen, Auftraggebern und ausführenden Firmen zusammen.
Kenntnisse in HOAI, VOB sowie einschlägigen Normen und technischen Regelwerken sind von Vorteil. Entscheidend ist für uns aber vor allem, dass du technisch stark bist, pragmatisch denkst und Lust hast, dich fachlich weiterzuentwickeln.

Gute Projekte entstehen nicht nur durch Technik, sondern vor allem durch Menschen, die gerne zusammenarbeiten. Deshalb ist uns wichtig, dass du bei DriveCon nicht einfach nur deine Aufgaben abarbeitest, sondern dich fachlich einbringen, weiterentwickeln und auf dein Team verlassen kannst.
Du bist Teil des Ganzen

Projekte, an denen du wachsen kannst

Weiterentwicklung, die zu dir passt

Kurze Wege statt langer Abstimmungsschleifen

Unkompliziertes Miteinander

Die Stiftung Jugendsozialwerk Blaues Kreuz BL ist im Auftrag von öffentlichen und privaten Institutionen im Bereich der Jugend- und Sozialarbeit tätig. Wir engagieren uns in der Jugend- und Familienarbeit, in der Sucht- und Präventionsarbeit und in der sozialen und beruflichen Integration. Das Jugendsozialwerk besteht aus drei Fachbereichen: Arbeitsintegration, Wohnintegration und Kind.Jugend.Familie KJF.
Die Wohn- und Arbeitsintegration Bernhardsberg in Oberwil BL bietet vor allem für psychisch beeinträchtigte, junge Erwachsene vorübergehende Wohn- und Arbeitsmöglichkeiten. Die Angebote dienen der Rehabilitation von Menschen in schwierigen Lebenssituationen. Die Arbeit richtet sich nach sozialpädagogischen Grundsätzen, die Lebensbewältigung und Reintegration beinhalten
Auf dem Bernhardsberg suchen wir ab Dezember 2026 oder nach Vereinbarung eine
## Stv. Bereichsleitung Wohnintegration 80 % (Bernhardsberg, Oberwil) ##
Ihre Aufgaben
* Aktive Mitverantwortung für den Bereich in verschiedenen Teilaufgaben (Finanzen/ Budget, Personalführung, Organisation, Infrastruktur, Qualitätssicherung usw.) und Stellvertretung der Bereichsleitung bei Abwesenheit
* Mitarbeit im Aufnahmeverfahren (In-Take) von neuen Klienten-innen
* Entwicklung und Evaluation der Angebote hinsichtlich Zweckmässigkeit und Effizienz
* Vertretung in relevanten Kommissionen, Arbeitsgruppen und gegenüber Behörden
* Bezugspersonenarbeit
Ihr Profil
* Abgeschlossene Ausbildung im Sozialbereich (FH/HF) mit Berufserfahrung
* Verwurzelt im christlichen Glauben
* Hohe Sozialkompetenz, Empathie, Belastbarkeit und Organisationstalent
* Engagierte, tatkräftige und glaubwürdige Führungspersönlichkeit
* Ein Herz für Menschen in schwierigen Lebenslagen
* Branchenerfahrung (Sozialpädagogik) im Bereich des stationären Wohnens
* Mehrere Jahre Führungserfahrung und betriebswirtschaftliche Kenntnisse (von Vorteil)
* Bereitschaft betriebsrelevante Weiterbildungen zu absolvieren
Unser Angebot
* Übernahme einer verantwortungsvollen Position mit Gestaltungsfreiraum
* Eine Herausforderung, die sinnstiftend ist und das Leben von Menschen nachhaltig zum Positiven verändern kann
* Gute Anstellungsbedingungen und eine soziale Arbeitgeberin
* Möglichkeit zur Weiterbildung
* Eigene Betriebskantine
* Attraktiver Arbeitsplatz (naturnah und trotzdem gut erschlossen)
* TNW öV Job-Ticket
Toleranz, Menschlichkeit und ein Hohes Mass an Miteinander sind uns wichtig. Mit unserem Leitbild können Sie sich identifizieren.
